transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that ever since I stopped working, I just can't seem to slow down. I'm up and moving from one little job to the next all day long. It's almost like I still have a crew waiting on me to get things done, even though I'm retired.
How has your sleep been lately?

My sleep? It's been fine, really. I haven't noticed any problems with it. I usually just hit the pillow and I'm out. I still wake up pretty early, same as I always did when I was working, but... yeah, I sleep okay.
Have you been feeling unusually high, excited, or overly cheerful lately?
No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I've been feeling unusually high or excited or anything like that. I'm just... busy, I guess. But my mood is pretty normal, same as always.
Do you feel like you need less sleep than usual?

No, not at all. I still need my regular amount of rest. Like I said, I wake up early, but I go to bed at a normal time, too. It's not like I'm running on just a couple hours of sleep or anything like that. I definitely still need a full night's rest.
Do you feel driven to repeat certain actions or routines, even when you know they aren’t necessary?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have my regular daily habits, just like anyone else, but... I don't feel forced to do things over and over. If I know something doesn't need doing, I just leave it be. So, no, nothing like that.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things most days?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal concerns like anybody else my age, but... I don't spend my days worrying about a bunch of different things. I just kind of take things as they come, to be honest.
Do you often feel on edge or like you have to stay alert for danger?
No, I don't have that problem at all. I feel pretty relaxed, really. I'm not looking over my shoulder or expecting something bad to happen. I just go about my day.
Do you feel physically restless or unable to sit still?

Yeah, I do actually. If I'm sitting through something quiet, like... well, a church talk or a meeting, I just feel like I've got to shift around. I'll end up tapping my foot, or I just feel this urge to get up and stretch, even when I know I really should just stay put.
Has this restlessness been a new change for you, or has it always been part of how you are?

It's pretty much always been part of who I am. Not a new change at all. I mean, even way back in grade school, my teachers used to say I was a bright kid, but just... scattered. I was always losing my pencils, or calling out answers in class. They constantly had to give me reminders to actually finish my work before I could go out for recess. So, yeah, it's been a lifelong thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation. The patient reports lifelong restlessness, difficulty sitting still, foot tapping, and a chronic history since grade school of being scattered, losing items, calling out in class, and needing frequent reminders to finish work. There is no evidence of mania, anxiety, OCD, or a new-onset condition, and the symptoms began in childhood with persistent course into adulthood.
